item.title: Geoflaw: Geofeed Errors, Inconsistencies, and Flaws
item.description: arXiv:2611.33365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geofeeds allow IP address resource owners to self-publish the geolocation of their prefixes, and adoption has grown substantially: as of November 2026, more than 5,000 geofeeds cover 1.6M prefixes. We measure geofeed errors, inconsistencies, and flaws by collecting geofeed references from the WHOIS of all five RIRs weekly over three months and downloading every referenced geofeed. The share of WHOIS objects complying with RFC 9632, which specifies how inetnum objects reference geofeeds, drops from 90% to 61%, driven by a single operator's objects with multiple geofeed references. Each week, 12-20% of geofeed URLs cannot be downloaded, and one in five downloaded geofeeds violates RFC 8805, which defines the geofeed CSV format. Moreover, 17% of geofeeds list IPv4 prefixes whose WHOIS object references a different geofeed. Finally, 281k prefixes appear in more than one geofeed, 3.8k of them with conflicting locations, and for 26% of these conflicts no geofeed is authoritative. We publish our results on a public dashboard, which one large CDN has already used to fix its geofeeds.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Gasser, Robert Beverly

item.title: A Global Solver for Minimum-Time Connectivity Restoration in UAV Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.33855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Node failures can split an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network into disconnected groups. Restoring communication requires moving the surviving aircraft, and the operator needs both an executable movement plan and an assessment of how much shorter the recovery could be. We develop Connectivity Restoration Branch-and-Bound (CR-BB), which returns a feasible plan and numerical displacement bounds; dividing these bounds by the common speed gives the corresponding time interval. Exact-arithmetic guarantees are established by the theorems. When the gap is not closed, the plan is feasible but not certified optimal. A fixed-tree subproblem is a second-order cone program. CR-BB searches over spanning trees and uses a Joint Mandatory-Link Bound (JMLB) to remove tree families that cannot improve the incumbent; Progress-based Adaptive Stopping (PAS) controls the search budget. On 200 matched cases, enabling the JMLB in the branch bound raised the number of cases meeting the prescribed displacement gap from 182 to 200 and reduced mean expanded nodes from 49.6 to 0.7. On a 60-case exact comparison, CR-BB met the gap in 90.0% of cases, compared with 55.0% for a spanning-tree mixed-integer conic formulation and 37.5% of the eight runs completed by an independent optimizer. On 1,000 paired recovery cases, CR-BB planned first restored connectivity in 72.35 steps on average, compared with 124.32 for an edge-augmentation baseline with conic refinement, a 41.8% reduction; on the common 50% subset the reduction was 28.1%. Across 2,466 cases, PAS reduced cumulative solver time by 20.9% and expanded nodes by 31.1% relative to a fixed search budget, with a 0.36-step mean increase in planned steps; most of the saving came from cases where neither configuration met the gap, and 60 plans became longer.
item.dc:creator: Huan Lin, Lianghui Ding

item.title: MoS: Mixture-of-Modality Streaming for Low-Latency Online Video LLM Analytics over Dynamic Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.33898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The serving model for next-generation video analytics systems is shifting from traditional task-specific vision models to general-purpose online video Large Language Models (LLMs). Online video LLMs enable flexible, contextual understanding of continuously arriving video content via natural language. However, their substantial resource requirements typically mandate cloud-based inference, making continuous video streaming from user devices necessary to keep the cloud model's context current for online interaction. This introduces significant challenges under existing dynamic and often harsh networks, degrading both accuracy and responsiveness in latency-sensitive applications. In this paper, we propose MoS, a new streaming system that adaptively streams a combination of visual and derived textual modalities over fluctuating networks to enable Pareto-optimal video LLM analytics. The key insight is to leverage the complementarity and interchangeability of different modalities, hidden in video LLM, to improve system performance. Concretely, MoS introduces adaptive anchor frame selection and incremental content tracking to enable low-latency text description generation at the device side. A joint profiler characterizes the accuracy and overhead of paired video and textual configurations, including caption input resolution and output-token budget. A stochastic optimization-based modality controller then selects modality combinations and configurations using this profile and the asynchronous latency of the two modalities to adapt to network conditions. Across 500 StreamingBench video-question pairs, 4G/5G uplink traces, and the VideoLLM-Online and DisPider backends, MoS reduces latency violations by up to 94.3% and improves accuracy by up to 60.4% relative to the evaluated streaming baselines.
item.dc:creator: Zekai Li, Xiaoyi Fan, Yifei Zhu

item.title: A Nationwide Snapshot of Starlink Affordability
item.description: arXiv:2611.34050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Starlink positions itself as "fast affordable Internet" that can provide service to nearly every household in the United States, and is slated to be responsible for providing the only broadband service to a significant number of US households via the NTIA's BEAD program. However, neither the FCC's National Broadband Map nor Starlink's own availability map captures what service costs. We present the first national census of Starlink's residential broadband pricing. We first identify that Starlink's offers are uniform within H3 resolution 6 grid cells, allowing us to collect plans and prices for every populated cell in the United States, more than 162,000 addresses, in October 2026. We find that while Starlink's service prices are fairly consistent, the effective price of the most affordable plan varies across the country, driven by restricting sales of less expensive plans as well as "demand surcharges" ranging between \$100 and \$1,500. Using a common affordability threshold of 2% of monthly income, we find that service restrictions or surcharges make Starlink unaffordable for approximately 4.3 million households, and in total nearly a quarter of all US households (roughly 25.5 million) cannot afford Starlink. Finally, approximately 80% of locations where Starlink is slated to receive BEAD funding face no constrained pricing today.
item.dc:creator: Shaddi Hasan

item.title: Evaluating Strategies for Multimodal Bidirectional Interactions between Pedestrians and AVs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) share spaces with Vulnerable Road Users (VRUs) in encounters where driver cues are absent. This can leave people uncertain whether the vehicle has noticed them and understood their request. Existing research has studied how AVs communicate with pedestrians through external human-machine interfaces. This work investigates bidirectional multimodal VRU-AV interactions combining Augmented Reality (AR), speech, and gestures. The study follows four stages: literature synthesis of interactions, a survey with 124 participants, interaction loop implementation, and feasibility evaluation. Participants preferred AR cues that made vehicle motion or warnings explicit, high-level voice commands, and conventional gestures. Prototype measurements revealed a trade-off between faster local processing and more accurate infrastructure-assisted processing. The demonstration shows bidirectional interaction using AR wearables and vehicular communications, while leaving decision-making to the AV. Together, the results support treating AV-VRU interaction as a closed loop of intent expression, recognition, vehicle decision, and feedback.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e Cl\'erigo, Maximilian Schrapel, Pedro Rito, Susana Sargento, Alexey Vinel

item.title: Curated Collaborative AI Edge with Network Data Analytics for B5G/6G Radio Access Networks
item.description: arXiv:2507.01994v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite advancements, Radio Access Networks (RAN) still account for over 50\% of the total power consumption in 5G networks. Existing RAN split options do not fully harness data potential, presenting an opportunity to reduce operational expenditures. This paper addresses this opportunity through a twofold approach. First, highly accurate network traffic and user predictions are achieved using the proposed Curated Collaborative Learning (CCL) framework, which selectively collaborates with relevant correlated data for traffic forecasting. CCL optimally determines whom, when, and what to collaborate with, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art approaches, including global, federated, personalized federated, and cyclic institutional incremental learnings by 43.9%, 39.1%, 40.8%, and 31.35%, respectively. Second, the Distributed Unit Pooling Scheme (DUPS) is proposed, leveraging deep reinforcement learning and prediction inferences from CCL to reduce the number of active DU servers efficiently. DUPS dynamically redirects traffic from underutilized DU servers to optimize resource use, improving energy efficiency by up to 89% over conventional strategies, translating into substantial monetary benefits for operators. By integrating CCL-driven predictions with DUPS, this paper demonstrates a transformative approach for minimizing energy consumption and operational costs in 5G RANs, significantly enhancing efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
item.dc:creator: Sardar Jaffar Ali, Syed M. Raza, Duc-Tai Le, Min Young Chung, Ness Shroff, Hyunseung Choo

item.title: AI Lifecycle-Aware Feasibility Framework for Split-RIC Orchestration in NTN O-RAN
item.description: arXiv:2603.23252v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) is constrained by the joint limits of satellite Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP), feeder-link capacity, and orbital connectivity, which directly affect O-RAN closed-loop control and AI lifecycle management. This paper studies the feasibility of distributing the O-RAN intelligence across Ground, LEO, and GEO segments through three representative deployments: (i) Ground-Centric control with telemetry streaming, (ii) a ground-LEO Split-RIC with on-board inference and store-and-forward model refresh, and (iii) GEO-LEO multi-layer control enabled by inter-satellite links. For each deployment, we derive closed-form expressions for lifecycle energy, near-real-time control latency, and model-refresh latency, while explicitly enforcing power-feasible spaceborne computational throughput. Pairwise analytical boundaries and numerical sensitivity analysis over telemetry volume, feeder-link conditions, inference workload, model longevity, and orbital waiting time identify the operating regions in which different placements are energetically preferable or satisfy model-refresh requirements. The results show that the architecture choice is inherently lifecycle- and constraint-dependent, providing decision-enabling primitives for Service Management and Orchestration (SMO) level AI placement and lifecycle orchestration in NTN O-RAN.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Tarchi

item.title: Beyond the Next Hop: Measuring Data-Plane Forwarding for RPKI-Invalid Prefixes in the Wild
item.description: arXiv:2603.29207v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An operator can inspect local routing and forwarding tables to identify the next hop for a destination, but cannot tell toward which origin traffic is forwarded beyond that hop. We study this question for IPv6 prefixes with RPKI-invalid announcements in the wild. We develop a context-aware path association method that derives discriminative features near candidate origins from collector-visible BGP paths and uses them to infer forwarding directions from incomplete traceroutes. Across 82 measurement rounds, we collected 169.5 million traceroutes from 1,811 ASes toward 2,764 target prefixes. Our measurements show that traffic is less often forwarded toward invalid origins when non-invalid alternatives are available, with fewer than 10% of traceroutes showing forwarding exclusively toward invalid origins, compared with about a quarter without alternatives. Notably, when alternatives are absent, we find that prefixes with identifiable operational explanations retain substantially broader reachability than unexplained prefixes, suggesting that connectivity considerations may drive continued invalid-route propagation. Our case analyses further reveal how interconnection, filtering, and export policies shape the propagation and use of invalid routes, including collateral damage under partial ROV deployment. By looking beyond the locally selected next hop, our work bridges the gap between local route selection and actual downstream forwarding, uncovering operational blind spots that local routing data alone cannot reveal.
item.dc:creator: Renrui Tian, Yahui Li, Xingang Shi, Xiao Liu, Ying Tian, Yanbo Yin, Xinzhe Liu, Yuhang Li, Jiarui Li, Yujie Huang, Han Zhang, Zhiliang Wang, Xia Yin

item.title: Toward Realistic Wi-Fi Fault Diagnosis: A Multi-Modal Benchmark
item.description: arXiv:2605.22008v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Intelligent network operation and maintenance systems in modern networks continuously generate large volumes of multi-modal operational data. However, Wi-Fi fault diagnosis under heterogeneous operational environments remains insufficiently understood. We build a real-world Wi-Fi testbed deployed in campus working environments with an automated fault injection system, and collect a multi-modal Wi-Fi fault dataset containing over 10,000 fault samples across diverse wireless scenarios. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first publicly available datasets jointly capturing heterogeneous cross-layer operational observations for Wi-Fi fault diagnosis. Based on this dataset, we establish a unified benchmark spanning multiple diagnosis tasks, operational modalities, and representative diagnosis paradigms. Experimental results indicate that effectively leveraging heterogeneous operational data remains challenging for existing diagnosis approaches. We further evaluate emerging LLM-based approaches and develop a reasoningoriented evaluation framework to assess the consistency between generated diagnostic analyses and actual network conditions. Our findings suggest several important considerations for future multi-modal Wi-Fi diagnosis.
item.dc:creator: Junjian Zhang, Haobo Deng, Xinxin Li, Ming Zhao, Fengxiao Tang, Nei Kato

item.title: Prefix Visibility Ratio: Quantifying Partial Observability in Carpet Bombing Detection
item.description: arXiv:2610.29802v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Carpet bombing attacks distribute malicious traffic across many destinations within a network prefix, while operational monitoring commonly provides destination-specific telemetry for only a subset of those targets. This creates an attack-conditional observability problem that is not captured by address utilization or nominal monitoring coverage. We introduce the Prefix Visibility Ratio (PVR), defined as the fraction of attacked destinations for which the telemetry required by the host-level evidence plane is available, and argue that PVR should be treated as an explicit evaluation dimension for carpet bombing detection. We then present VANTA (Visibility-Aware Network Threat Analysis) as one concrete way to operationalize this principle. VANTA combines host-level and prefix-level anomaly scores, estimates PVR online from router-side destination evidence and the monitored-destination inventory, and adjusts evidence fusion according to both estimated visibility and estimator confidence. Across a validated campaign of 2,160 Mininet runs, VANTA achieves 99.18% precision, 93.46% recall, a global F1-score of 96.24%, and a 1.54% false-positive rate. In a separate matched-observability study using task-adapted feature-level reference implementations, VANTA reaches 95.89% pooled F1 and 92.39% recall for configured PVR<=10%, with its largest advantage appearing at configured PVR=1%. These reference comparisons are intended to isolate observability effects under a common binary detection task rather than to reproduce the original end-to-end objectives of the referenced systems. The results establish attacked-destination visibility as a measurable factor that can materially change detector behavior and should be reported explicitly in future carpet bombing evaluations.
item.dc:creator: Farid Na\"it-Abdesselam, Laaziz Lahlou, Doha Bentaoussy, Hugo Lege, Eve Lin, Nadjia Kara

item.title: Martingale-Based Resource Partitioning Bounds for URLLC and eMBB Network Slicing in 5G
item.description: arXiv:2610.36602v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Network slicing enables the coexistence of ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC) and enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) in 5G networks. However, provisioning limited radio resources under stochastic traffic and wireless service while satisfying heterogeneous quality-of-service (QoS) requirements remains challenging. This paper proposes a martingale-based resource block (RB) allocation framework for coexisting URLLC and eMBB slices. Under the stated independence assumptions, exponential martingales are constructed using the moment generating functions of the arrival and service processes. By applying Doob's maximal inequality, we derive analytical upper bounds on the URLLC virtual-delay violation probability and the eMBB backlog violation probability. These bounds provide sufficient QoS conditions for resource allocation. A bisection procedure determines the martingale parameters, followed by an integer search for the minimum RB allocations certified by the derived bounds. Numerical results show that the proposed bounds are tighter than an optimized Chernoff--union baseline in the evaluated scenario.
item.dc:creator: Hanbing Li, Wenyang Ji, Yi Zhou, Hao Ma, Yantong Wang

item.title: Budgeted Decision-Model-Guided Joint-Action Search for Satellite Edge Computing
item.description: arXiv:2611.19225v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Efficient task offloading in satellite edge computing requires coordinated allocation of communication and computing resources. Search methods based on large language models (LLMs) have been shown to generate high-quality resource allocations, but the latency of individual model requests and repeated model interactions can lead to substantial solver overhead. We propose budgeted joint-action search (BJAS), an integrated decision-model-guided solver that jointly optimizes satellite offloading and power allocation to minimize average task-completion latency under explicit search budgets. Its bounded candidate pools combine single-terminal updates with power-inheriting offload replacements for batched selection, retaining two-terminal coordination without enumerating additional power vectors. Across 60 completed runs per method under the workflows' respective configurations, BJAS reduces mean total solver time by 97.16% relative to LLM-generated offloading while achieving a mean task-completion latency close to that of the LLM baseline. BJAS also achieves lower mean task-completion latency than the tested genetic algorithm and deep deterministic policy gradient baselines.
item.dc:creator: Ziming Liu, Minghao Sun, Ran Tao, Xiaoli Chu

item.title: EdgeNet City: Context-Aware AI-RAN Planning toward Autonomous Urban Connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.19231v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The evolution from 5G toward 6G calls for more anticipatory and context-aware Cell-on-Wheels (COW) planning in wireless networks. We present EdgeNet City, an online framework that grounds free-form natural-language inputs in geographic activity representations and path-gain data. A catalog-referenced representation links activity roles, geographic features and predefined demand profiles, separating semantic selection from deterministic spatial computation. The algorithm combines prescribed demand with relative propagation support to screen service areas for subsequent COW assessment. We publicly release a London dataset with 22,678 transmitters, approximately 449.4 billion path-gain records and retained receiver geometry. Within prepared propagation domains, the online prototype reuses these records without new ray tracing or live operator measurements. In a matched 20-event study across six London environments, the expanded representation increases mean spatial overlap with the reused full technical-review reference from 0.4929 for the single-feature Venue-only baseline to 0.7203. Rule-based and language-model planners select identical activities in this panel. With need-aware ranking and a three-cell diagnostic budget fixed, the expanded representation increases mean Reference-need Capture by 25.44 percentage points over Venue-only.
item.dc:creator: Ziming Liu, Boxuan Shan, Qixing Deng, Wenchao Xue, Xiaoli Chu

item.title: Intelligence as a Founding Principle: The O-RAN Architecture for Artificial Intelligence and Its Reference Implementations
item.description: arXiv:2611.28282v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Since its inception, O-RAN has established openness and intelligence as founding principles of the RAN, transforming closed base stations into disaggregated, multi-vendor systems with a hierarchical RIC. This article traces AI/ML in O-RAN through open specifications and reference implementations to 6G design. We examine how open fronthaul, RIC interfaces, cloud orchestration, and AAL profiles support control loops across multiple timescales, model management, and hardware acceleration. Commercial deployments and OTIC testing demonstrate multi-vendor interoperability. Open-source stacks and testbeds support pre-standardization studies of in-node dApps. Within this architecture, GPU-based AI-RAN platforms realize the inline High-PHY split on shared RAN and AI compute, providing one reference implementation path for the O-RAN AAL alongside other implementations on heterogeneous hardware. Vector instruction sets and analog in-memory computing offer longer-term options for improving energy efficiency. For 6G, extending intelligence to time-critical radio processing and mobile agent services calls for deadline-bounded third-party inference, energy-efficient RAN/Edge-AI silicon co-design, and agent session continuity across handovers. We propose a RAC that coordinates agents across tiers through local shells and a shared exposure gateway, with in-node operating bounds delivered asynchronously. We also propose Recursive Standardization, in which results from federated open labs inform candidate 6G requirements and standards review guides the next round of implementation and testing.
item.dc:creator: Chih-Lin I, Hao Xu, Tao Chen, Frank H. P. Fitzek, Muhammad Ali Imran, Sen Wang

item.title: Practical limitations on robustness and scalability of quantum Internet
item.description: arXiv:2308.12739v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The realization of a desirably functional quantum Internet is hindered by fundamental and practical challenges such as high loss during transmission of quantum systems, decoherence due to interaction with the environment, fragility of quantum states under measurement, etc. We study the implications of these constraints by analyzing the limitations on the scaling and robustness of the quantum Internet. Considering quantum networks, we present practical bottlenecks for secure communication, delegated computing, and resource distribution among end nodes. In particular, we show that the device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) network of isotropic states with parameter $p$ has a finite diameter depending on $p$. Motivated by the power of abstraction in graph theory (in association with quantum information theory), that allows us to consider the topology of a network of users spatially separated over long distances around the globe or separated as nodes within the small space over a processor or circuit within a same framework, we consider graph-theoretic quantifiers to assess network robustness and provide critical values of communication lines for viable communication over quantum Internet. We consider some quantum networks of practical interest, ranging from satellite-based networks connecting far-off spatial locations to currently available quantum processor architectures within computers, and analyze their robustness to perform quantum information processing tasks. Some of these tasks form primitives for delegated quantum computing, e.g., entanglement distribution and quantum teleportation, that are desirable for all scale of quantum networks, be it quantum processors or quantum Internet.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Sadhu, Meghana Ayyala Somayajula, Karol Horodecki, Siddhartha Das

item.title: The Bilateral Efficiency of Ethernet: Recalibrating Metcalfe and Boggs After Fifty Years
item.description: arXiv:2603.19406v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In July 1976, Metcalfe and Boggs published their foundational paper on Ethernet in Communications of the ACM. Their efficiency model -- E = (P/C)/(P/C + W*T) -- measures the fraction of Ether time carrying good forward packets under contention. For fifty years this model has framed how the community thinks about Ethernet performance. We argue it is silent on the question that matters for modern intra-rack interconnect: bilateral transaction efficiency -- the fraction of link time that produces committed agreements between sender and receiver. Metcalfe and Boggs themselves planted the seed in their EFTP "end-dally" protocol (Section 7.2.2), and the deeper anchor is older still: Abramson's Alohanet carried positive acknowledgments at the link layer -- a bilateral mechanism Metcalfe consciously removed in 1973 to obtain Ethernet's simple, ACK-free packet format. The result is a fifty-year bilateral zigzag: Aloha (bilateral) to Ethernet (unilateral) to the EFTP end-dally (bilateral) to TCP (unilateral-with-bilateral-above). We formalize bilateral efficiency, connect it to the back-to-back Shannon channel with Perfect Information Feedback, and -- scoping the claim explicitly to intra-rack distances of one meter or less -- describe how the Open Aethernet link recovers mutual knowledge at the link layer. The correction to Table 1 is not a different set of numbers. It is a different question. A new appendix places the 2025-2026 return of link-level retry (UEC, OCP ESUN, UALink) in this history and shows that it restores half of the end-dally: the sender learns of delivery, the receiver never learns that the sender knows. It opens from Ron Crane's observation that produced Fast Ethernet: carried to 100 Gb/s, the same arithmetic makes the minimum frame about one meter long.
item.dc:creator: Paul Borrill

item.title: Secure Quantum Handshakes: Quantum Network Verification Via Simon's Algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2610.12209v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum networking represents the future of secure communication, enabling fundamentally new capabilities through quantum information exchange. However, these networks require secure, high-fidelity quantum communication channels. Currently, there is no reliable method to verify whether clients entering a quantum network truly possess quantum state communication capability over robust channels. In this work, we introduce a client-validation protocol that functions as a proof-of-quantum-communication handshake. Our protocol secures a quantum network against classical spoofers, faulty quantum computers, and genuine quantum devices connecting to the network over noisy or insecure channels. We validate the efficacy of this protocol through numerical simulations under erasure, dephasing, and depolarizing noise models.
item.dc:creator: Reece Robertson, Sejal Patil, Sebastian Deffner
